summary: Complete scoped planning pass with thirteen declaration-sized additions and five accepted P7 imports. Reuses pinned finite ideal-power quotients and adic uniform continuity, derives finite-free precompleteness from the pinned completion API, and imports R03.1 completion Noetherianity. The finite unframed arithmetic theorem and framing presentation stay with their owners. Two explicit interface gaps remain; no implementation or proof closure is claimed.

nodes.title: Finite residual fibre over a complete local subring
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative local ring complete for m_A, and B a Noetherian commutative local A-algebra whose coefficient map is local. If B/m_A B is finite as an A-module (equivalently as a k_A-vector space), then B is finite as an A-module. The target need not be complete and the coefficient map need not be injective.
hypotheses: A is m_A-adically complete, including separatedness.
B is Noetherian local; A→B is local.
The residual fibre is finite-dimensional; its equality with k_B is not assumed.
proofSteps: Choose finitely many lifts in B of generators of B/m_A B and form the A-linear map A^r→B. Its composite with the quotient is surjective.

For finite-free precompleteness, use piEquivFin to identify completion(A^r) with completion(A)^r. Choose a preimage in A of each coordinate using of_surjective. The identities piEquivFin_apply and map_of show that their tuple maps to the original completion element. Injectivity of the equivalence and of_surjective_iff give precompleteness of A^r. In current Tau Ceti this step is already IsPrecomplete.pi and must be reused.
Since m_A B⊆m_B, Noetherian local separation of B over B and IsHausdorff.of_map give m_A-Hausdorffness as an A-module. The finite B-module used here is B itself, not a hypothesized finite A-module.
Apply surjective_of_mkQ_comp_surjective, then Module.Finite.of_surjective. No target completeness or coefficient-map injection is used.
acceptance: Test B=A, B=A/I for a proper ideal, and B=A[[X]]: the first two satisfy the criterion; the last has infinite residual fibre.
Removing Noetherian local separation must leave a stated Hausdorff hypothesis; never infer separation from desired finiteness.

sources.match: Derived ring specialization of native topological Nakayama; the finite-coordinate precompleteness step follows from the same pinned completion API.

sources.locator: AdicCompletion.piEquivFin, piEquivFin_apply and map_of, lines 340–364 and 187–188
sources.match: Finite-coordinate transport supplies the source precompleteness without a new planned library lemma.
Converts the coordinatewise surjectivity argument into precompleteness.

nodes.title: Finiteness for the completed local rings
nodes.statement: Let A,B be Noetherian local commutative rings and let Â,B̂ be their maximal-ideal completions. Given a local algebra map Â→B̂ with B̂/m_Â B̂ finite over Â, B̂ is finite over Â. Noetherianity of B̂ is imported from R03.1/completion-noetherian. For an initial local map A→B, the induced completed map and comparison of residual fibres remain explicit R03.1 interface obligations.
hypotheses: The algebra structure between completions is specified, not inferred from two independent algebra structures.
Noetherianity of B̂ follows from the accepted R03.1 completion theorem applied to the finitely generated maximal ideal of B; it is not inferred from completeness alone.
proofSteps: Use baseline locality and maximal-ideal completeness for Â and B̂. Use R03.1/completion-noetherian for B̂: m_B is finitely generated and B/m_B is Noetherian.
Apply the preceding residual-fibre criterion to the declared local map of completions.

To use a map A→B, import its continuous extension and the comparison B̂/m_A B̂≅B/m_A B when the latter is finite-dimensional; this comparison is an owner obligation, not an extra hypothesis erased in a prototype.
acceptance: The Lean signature specifies the local algebra map between completions. It does not separately assume Noetherianity of B̂, whose planned supplier is cited directly.
A completion does not make the infinite residual fibre of A[[X]] finite.

sources.match: Combines existing completeness/locality with the new finiteness criterion; does not read Noetherianity into the module header.

nodes.title: Finite DVR algebra and its special fibre
nodes.statement: Let O be a complete DVR with finite residue field k and A a Noetherian local O-algebra with local coefficient map. Then A is module-finite over O iff A/πA has finite cardinality, where π is any uniformizer. No flatness is asserted.
hypotheses: The residue field is finite; O is complete.
π generates m_O; A need not be O-flat or reduced.
proofSteps: For finite A, quotient finiteness descends and scalars factor through k, so the special fibre is a finite k-module and hence a finite set.

For a finite special fibre, its whole carrier is a finite spanning set over O. Submodule.fg_span and Module.finite_def give finite generation over O. Apply the residual-fibre criterion and replace m_O A by πA. The finite coefficient ring is required only in the forward implication.
acceptance: O/π² is allowed and is not flat.
k is finite over O but supplies no characteristic-zero point.
Keep cardinal finiteness distinct from module finiteness in signatures.

sources.match: The conversion is made over the finite residue field, rather than over the infinite DVR.
A finite carrier gives a finite spanning set over O; no finite-cardinality hypothesis on O is needed.
Identifies a finite spanning set with module finiteness.

nodes.title: Finiteness from a faithful finite patched module
nodes.statement: Let S be a Noetherian commutative ring, R a commutative S-algebra and M an R-module with a compatible S-module structure and commuting scalar actions. If M is finite over S and faithful over R, then R is finite over S. For KW II, S=O[[y₁,…,y_{h+j}]].
hypotheses: S is Noetherian.
The action R→End_S(M) is S-linear and faithful; finiteness over R alone is insufficient.
proofSteps: The native Algebra.lsmul action gives R→ₐ[S]End_S(M). Faithfulness makes this map injective by evaluating equality on each vector.
End_S(M) is Noetherian over S by the existing Hom theorem. Apply Module.Finite.of_injective to the action map.
This retains the integrated node ID only for its faithful-module assertion; its former cardinal, completed and arithmetic assertions are separated or imported.
acceptance: A finite nonfaithful module must not force R finite: k=R/(π,X) for R=O[[X]].
The zero module works only for the zero ring R under faithfulness.
No freeness, flatness or patching arithmetic is asserted.

sources.locator: §9.1, printed p.88, after the patching limit
sources.match: The faithful-module argument in the source; the statement generalizes its coefficient ring to any Noetherian S.

nodes.title: A zero-dimensional Noetherian local ring with finite residue field is finite
nodes.statement: If R is Noetherian local of Krull dimension at most zero and k_R is finite, then R has finite cardinality.
hypotheses: Noetherian local R, finite residue field, KrullDimLE 0 R.
Completeness and a coefficient-field embedding are not required.
proofSteps: Dimension zero and Noetherianity give Artinianity by the pinned theorem.

Its maximal ideal is nilpotent. Choose n with m^n=0 and identify R with R/m^n. Noetherianity makes m finitely generated; Ideal.finite_quotient_pow supplies finite cardinality of the quotient directly.
acceptance: Nonreduced rings such as Z/9Z satisfy the conclusion.
Finite residue field without dimension zero fails for k[[X]].

sources.match: Adds finite cardinality by the finite maximal-ideal filtration; does not replan the existing Artinianity theorem.
Reuses the existing quotient-power theorem instead of planning another finite-filtration lemma.

nodes.title: Finite prime quotients imply finiteness of a local ring
nodes.statement: If R is Noetherian local and R/q has finite cardinality for every prime ideal q, then R has finite cardinality.
hypotheses: Noetherian local R; all prime quotients finite, including the maximal quotient.
proofSteps: A prime quotient is a finite domain and hence a field. Thus every prime of R is maximal and its Krull dimension is at most zero.
The hypothesis at m_R gives a finite residue field. Apply the previous lemma.
acceptance: This isolates the commutative-algebra tail of the finite-image trace argument; trace generation and torsion eigenvalues remain with the Galois owner.

sources.match: The source concludes finite prime quotients, then dimension zero and finiteness; this node makes the last implication explicit.
Converts the verified field-quotient condition into dimension zero.

nodes.title: Positive dimension detects a surviving uniformizer
nodes.statement: Let O be a DVR and A a finite local O-algebra with local coefficient map. For a uniformizer π, 1≤dim A iff π_A is not nilpotent.
hypotheses: The coefficient map is local, so π_A lies in m_A.
A is module-finite over O. No reducedness, torsion-freeness or completeness is assumed.
proofSteps: Nilpotent π_A makes A Artinian by the accepted predecessor; Artinian rings have dimension at most zero.

Conversely, if dim A<1 then the extended-natural dimension inequality gives dim A≤0. A is Noetherian because O is Noetherian and A finite, so it is Artinian. Its maximal ideal is nilpotent, and π_A lies in that ideal by locality.
acceptance: For A=k or O/π² the left side fails.
A=O[ε]/ε² has a surviving π and is permitted.
Coefficient locality is explicit so that π_A belongs to m_A; no such dimension equivalence is asserted for arbitrary nonfinite algebras.

sources.match: The reverse direction uses maximal-ideal nilpotence, not a nonexistent torsion-free consequence.

nodes.title: Characteristic-zero integral point from a surviving uniformizer
nodes.statement: Let O be a DVR, K its fraction field of characteristic zero, Ω an algebraically closed K-extension, and A a finite local O-algebra with local coefficient map. If π_A is not nilpotent, there exist a finite intermediate field E/K in Ω and a local O-algebra map A→integralClosure(O,E), whose target is finite over O. This is the algebraic unit-reflecting point; no topology or fixed target residue field is part of this conclusion.
hypotheses: All O→K→Ω scalar towers commute.
π is a uniformizer and π_A is not nilpotent.
proofSteps: Use the preceding dimension equivalence and apply the accepted point theorem without altering its carrier or scalar towers.
For the direct construction, the accepted generic-prime, algebraic-point and finite-field-of-values nodes supply its internal steps; no new copies of those nodes are created.
acceptance: A=k and O/π² fail the hypothesis.
A=O is a point over K.
A=O[t]/(t(t−π)) has two branches; reduction alone does not distinguish their characteristic-zero points.

sources.match: The source uses finiteness and positive dimension to choose a generic prime avoiding p; our formulation allows any uniformizer.

nodes.title: A point in the integers of a finite local-field extension
nodes.statement: Let K be a characteristic-zero nonarchimedean local field, O=𝒪[K], Ω an algebraically closed K-extension, and A a finite local O-algebra with 1≤dim A. There is a finite E:IntermediateField K Ω, equipped with the induced finite-extension valuation and topology from LocalFieldsRamification Layer 0, and a local continuous O-algebra map A→𝒪[E]. The source has its maximal-adic topology and 𝒪[E] its induced local-field topology. Its residue field is allowed to extend that of A.
hypotheses: The actual integer-ring comparison is an O-algebra equivalence integralClosure(O,E)≃𝒪[E].
The finite-extension topology is constructed on E, not postulated as an arbitrary topology.
The coefficient map O→A is local, as in the inherited point theorem.
proofSteps: Apply the accepted algebraic point theorem with O=𝒪[K].

Reuse the actual finite IntermediateField structures already implemented in current Tau Ceti and exposed by LocalFieldsRamification Layer 0. Compose the algebraic point with the inverse of integerRingEquivIntegralClosure, with the O-algebra structure specified. Equivalences reflect units, so locality is preserved.

Derive the agreement of the induced integer-ring topology with its maximal-adic topology from the supplier maximal-ideal-power neighborhood basis, then specialize native adic uniform continuity using the local-map maximal-ideal inclusion. A named transport interface and its compatibility with the historical baseline are still to be checked.
acceptance: At the historical pins the prototype checks only transport through a genuine AlgEquiv. Current Tau Ceti provides the field structures and integer-ring comparison; upstream packaging must reuse them and complete the explicit topology adapter.
For Z₃[t]/(t²−18), any point forces the unit t/3 to have square 2; a target residue field equal to F₃ is impossible.

sources.match: Imports the existing roadmap’s ownership of finite-extension structures and comparison, rather than replanning them.

nodes.title: Locality of a compatible Artinian limit map
nodes.statement: Let B be an A-algebra and E a complete local A-algebra. For a compatible family f_n:B→E/m_E^n of A-algebra maps, if f_1 reflects units then the native lifted map B→E reflects units. Its reductions are exactly f_n.
hypotheses: Compatibility is equality after the canonical quotient maps for every m≤n.
E is m_E-adically complete, including Hausdorffness.
proofSteps: Use the existing liftAlgHom and its reduction identity at n=1.
The composite of the lift with E→E/m_E is f_1; apply isLocalHom_of_comp. No new inverse-limit carrier or existence theorem is introduced.
acceptance: The level n=0 is the zero ring and gives no locality information.
Only one compatible family can be realized; separately chosen lifts at each n are insufficient.

sources.match: The existing equality at level 1 allows the existing composite-locality criterion.

nodes.title: A local continuous framed point from Artinian lifting
nodes.statement: Let A→B be a local continuous formally smooth morphism in the complete Noetherian local coefficient category, and f:A→O′ a local continuous point in a complete DVR target after the required finite residue-field extension. Given a compatible local residue point B→O′/m′ over f, there exists a local continuous lift B→O′ over f. The R03.1 lifting interface must apply to the O′/m′^n tower after residue change. Equivalently the concrete consumer takes an initial local algebra map at level 1 and local successor lifts over the canonical quotient maps.
hypotheses: A and B are objects of the declared complete-local category.
Formal smoothness is tested on the actual target quotient category after compatible residue change.
A starting residue map and compatibility with f are supplied. Bare algebraic formal smoothness without these inputs is not the asserted hypothesis.
proofSteps: Use R03.1/positive-truncation for the Artinian quotients and small successor maps, and continuous-formal-smoothness for lifting in the declared residue-labelled category. The finite residue change and starting point must first make this the actual target category. For a DVR the positive successor kernels are one-dimensional over its residue field.

Starting with the given local level-1 point, use R03.1/compatible-lift-tower for dependent recursive choice of local successor lifts. The supplier gives compatibility after all composites and preserves the initial point; add the unique level-0 map.
Apply the native complete-target lift. Its A-algebra structure ensures the extension of f. Apply locality at level 1 and the native adic continuity theorem.
acceptance: The native signature exposes the concrete AlgHom successor-lifting quantifier; it does not define a new Prop containing the desired conclusion.
The lift preserves the chosen residue point. No fixed original residue field is promised.

sources.match: The proof uses the complete-local category’s lifting squares; this node spells out compatibility and the complete limit.

nodes.title: Framed point from a power series presentation
nodes.statement: Let A,B,E be commutative local rings, B an A-algebra, f:A→E a local ring map defining the A-algebra structure on E, and e:B≃ₐ[A]A[[X₁,…,X_d]]. Then B has a local continuous A-algebra map to E obtained by sending every X_i to zero. The presentation, when needed for deformation rings, comes from GlobalGaloisDeformations; this lemma does not prove it.
hypotheses: The presentation is an actual A-algebra equivalence.
Both topologies are the respective maximal-adic topologies.
d=0 is included. No completeness of E is needed for zero evaluation.
proofSteps: Compose e with constant-coefficient evaluation and then f. Constant-coefficient evaluation is A-linear and multiplicative by the native API.
The power series unit criterion and locality of f show that the composite reflects units. Apply native adic uniform continuity with the maximal ideals.
acceptance: For d=0 this is the base point.
Each framing variable has image zero.
Zero evaluation is continuous in maximal-adic topologies even when E is not complete.

sources.match: Uses the native constant coefficient map and its unit criterion, so no new power series evaluator is defined.

nodes.title: Positive framing variables prevent module finiteness
nodes.statement: For any nontrivial commutative O-algebra A and d>0, A[[X₁,…,X_d]] is not finite as an O-module. Thus a nonzero finite unframed O-algebra acquires points under framing, but loses O-module finiteness when at least one framing variable is added.
hypotheses: A is nontrivial; no Noetherianity or completeness is needed.
The O-algebra structure on the power series ring is the constant-coefficient one.
proofSteps: If the power series ring were O-finite, its variable X₁ would be integral over O. Choose a monic polynomial relation.

In its evaluation at X₁, the coefficient at the monic polynomial’s degree in the X₁ direction is 1_A: all lower-degree terms have zero coefficient there. This contradicts the relation being zero and 1_A≠0.
acceptance: A=0 is excluded.
d=0 is excluded and can be finite.
A=k with d=1 is the simplest counterexample to transferring unframed finiteness to the framed ring.

Imported the exact accepted R03.1/completion-noetherian node and removed redundant completion Noetherianity from the signature. The induced completed map and finite residual-fibre comparison remain explicitly requested.

Added finite spanning-set prerequisites for the reverse implication. The forward cardinality conversion is over the finite residue field; no finiteness of the DVR or flatness of the algebra is inferred.
KW II §9.1.3 p.88 supplies the motivating faithful-module argument. The action embeds R into the Noetherian S-module End_S(M); all scalar-tower and commuting-action hypotheses are retained.
Replaced the duplicate quotient-power prerequisite by Ideal.finite_quotient_pow and finite generation of the maximal ideal. Artinianity and nilpotence reduce the ring to one finite quotient.
KW early Lemma 2.4 p.10 contains this algebraic tail. Finite prime quotients are fields, all primes are maximal, and the finite residue field and dimension-zero criterion give cardinal finiteness.

The accepted nilpotent-uniformizer theorem and pinned Artinian/dimension equivalences give both directions. Finiteness over the DVR supplies Noetherianity; locality puts the uniformizer in the maximal ideal.

Read the accepted P7 point statement and the Corollary 4.7 argument at printed pp.45–46. The reformulation preserves the finite algebra, characteristic-zero fraction field and commuting scalar towers; neither topology nor a fixed target residue field is added.

Made coefficient locality explicit and recorded the current implemented intermediate-field structures and integer-ring equivalence. The historical-pin signature is only AlgEquiv transport; the current-library topology adapter is an honest recorded gap.

The native reduction identity at level 1 and isLocalHom_of_comp prove unit reflection of the native lift. Existence and all reduction identities are reused, not replanned; level 0 alone would be insufficient.

Imported the three exact R03.1 smooth-lifting nodes. Their fixed-residue category does not automatically contain a finite residue extension: the starting point and compatible local successor contract remain explicit inputs and a supplier adaptation request.

Replaced the proposed continuity lemma by the stronger native adic theorem. An actual algebra equivalence and the native constant-coefficient unit criterion produce the point, even when E is incomplete and d=0.

A positive variable would be integral in a finite algebra. Its monic polynomial relation has coefficient 1 at the top variable degree, contradicting zero. Nontriviality and positive variable count are essential and explicit.
